title: Decommissioning & Destruction
description: Handle cleanup gracefully with OnDisable, OnDestroy, and OnApplicationQuit.

slides.title: Saying Goodbye 👋
slides.content:
# Disable and Destroy

Objects don't last forever. When they are removed or deactivated, Unity calls:
- **OnDisable()** – when the object is deactivated or the script is disabled.
- **OnDestroy()** – when the object is destroyed (scene unload, `Destroy()`, etc.).

These are the perfect places to clean up, unsubscribe from events, and release resources.

quizData.question: When is OnDisable called?

options.text: Only when the object is destroyed
When the object becomes inactive or its script is disabled

quizData.explanation: OnDisable is called when the GameObject or the component's enabled state changes to false.

slides.title: OnDisable() – Temporary Goodbye ⏸️
slides.content:
# Cleanup on Deactivation

Use `OnDisable()` to:
- Unsubscribe from events (so disabled objects don't receive updates).
- Stop coroutines started in OnEnable.
- Reset static references if this object was holding them.

```csharp
void OnEnable() { EventManager.OnGameOver += HandleGameOver; }
void OnDisable() { EventManager.OnGameOver -= HandleGameOver; }
```

Failing to unsubscribe can lead to null reference errors or memory leaks.

quizData.question: OnDisable is called only when the entire GameObject is destroyed.
quizData.explanation: It is also called when the object is simply deactivated or the script disabled.

slides.title: OnDestroy() – Permanent Goodbye 💥
slides.content:
# When the Object Ceases to Exist

`OnDestroy()` is called when:
- The object is destroyed via `Destroy(gameObject)`.
- The scene is unloaded and the object is not marked `DontDestroyOnLoad`.
- The application quits (but see OnApplicationQuit).

Use it to:
- Release unmanaged resources.
- Tell other systems that this object no longer exists.
- Save final data.

**Note**: OnDestroy may not be called on application quit; use `OnApplicationQuit()` for critical saves.

slides.title: OnApplicationQuit() 📴
slides.content:
# Final Exit

`OnApplicationQuit()` is called on all scripts when the game is closing (in builds and in Editor when Play mode stops).

- Use for saving player preferences, high scores.
- It's called before OnDestroy, but after other shutdown logic.
- Works reliably even in WebGL builds.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Unsubscribe to Avoid Zombie Listeners

Always pair OnEnable/OnDisable for event subscriptions. If you subscribe in Start, unsubscribe in OnDestroy. A common source of bugs is an object that's destroyed but still listening to an event.
